main_text.p: Sequenti die cataplasma similiter adhibet ex pane cocto in aqua mulsa, & contrito cū amygdalis amaris, aut serpyllo, aut menta, aut calamintha, aut ruta, & ad tres dies hoc facit. Et postea caput radit, & peucedani succo in aceto dissoluto, in quo sphondylii coctū est, illinit. Interpositis rursus aliquot diebus, & corpore refecto, antidoti ex colocynthide obolos nouem in aqua mulsa propinat. Rursus interpositis diebus antidotum iterat, deinde sternutatoriis utitur.

Post quinque, aut decem dies castorium in aqua mulsa præbet: & rursus interposito tempore centaurij & colocynthidis decoctum per clysterem infundit: deinde rursus hieram præbet, & consequenter pituitam per os & nares attrahentibus utitur, deinde sinapismum capiti adhibet. Tempestiue uti acrium efu præcipit. Epilepticis acetum mulsum scyllitico bibere iubet, & mel, in quo scylla cotabuerit, cochlearij mesura. Victus rationem præscribit, quæ incidendi ac attenuandi uim habet: proinde capares & salsamenta assidue in cibo ait competere. Alexander Trallianus ad inueteratum comitia lem morbum, qui a prauo humore originem ducit, catapotia exhibet, quibus nihil ualentius

page.notes: Printed text is set in roman with long s; the text was copied with the printer's spelling, including "cū" and "præbet". Several words were read at low resolution and are uncertain: "sphondylii" and "scyllitico" may carry errors; "cochlearij" and "mesura" are doubtful. The line "Alexander Trallianus" appears set as "xanderTrallianus" in the scan, with a missing letter at the line break; it is shown here as "Alexander Trallianus". The foot paragraph is empty and should be removed; no footnote text is printed on this page. Left-edge show-through and page edge are not transcribed. Note: the final line "lentius" is printed indented at the end of the last paragraph.
